1.1: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
1.2: The earth had no shape yet, and nothing was in its place. Darkness was over the deep waters. God’s Spirit was there, moving over it all.
1.3: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
1.4: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated the light from the darkness.
1.5: God named the light Day, and He named the darkness Night. Evening came, and morning followed—the first day.
1.6: Then God said, "Let there be a wide space between the waters, so that the waters are separated from one another."
1.7: So God made the wide space, and He separated the waters below the space from the waters above it.
1.8: God called the wide space Sky. Evening came, and morning followed—the second day.
1.9: Then God said, "Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear." And it was so.
1.10: God called the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters He called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
1.11: Then God said, "Let the earth grow grass, plants that make seed, and trees that grow fruit with seed in it, each according to its kind." And it was so.
1.12: The earth brought forth grass, plants that make seed, and trees that bear fruit with seed in it, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
